title: Number bonds to 10
examples: Can you show me the pairs that make ten?
If I have 3, what number do I need to make 10?

explain.say: Look at this picture. We are finding pairs that make ten.
Let us count on our fingers. If we use 2 fingers, we need 8 more to reach ten.
If you have 5 blocks, you need five more blocks to make a total of ten.
We can find the pairs by counting up. Three plus seven makes a perfect ten.
In real life, we use number bonds all the time. If you have ten stickers and give away three, you have seven left.
A common mistake is forgetting that the order does not matter. Two and eight is the same as eight and two.

faq.a: There are many pairs that add up to ten. You can count them all out together.
asks: Can you name some pairs for ten?

faq.q: Does the order of the numbers change the answer?
faq.a: No, the order does not change the answer. Two plus eight is the same as eight plus two.
asks: Is 2 plus 8 the same as 8 plus 2?
Does order matter when adding to ten?

faq.q: What is the easiest way to learn these pairs?
faq.a: Using your fingers or drawing dots can help you see the missing number. It is a fun way to learn.
asks: How can I remember all the pairs?
Can I use my hands to learn this?

faq.q: Do I have to learn all of them at once?
faq.a: No, you can learn them slowly over time. Practice makes these number bonds easy to remember.
asks: Is it okay if I forget some pairs?
How long will it take to learn this?

faq.q: What if the total is not ten?
faq.a: If the total is not ten, we are finding number bonds to that new number. We can learn them next.
asks: What if we want to make 12?
Can we do this for other numbers?

facts: The number 10 is a key number for number bonds.
Every number up to ten has a partner to make ten.
The pairs are always opposites, like one and nine.
Adding the same number twice makes a special pair, like five and five.

quiz.say: What number goes with 4 to make ten?
quiz.why: You need 6 because four plus six equals ten.

wrong.0: You might just write the total number you are aiming for.
wrong.1: You might only count up two more fingers.
wrong.3: You might think you add it to itself, but that makes eight.

quiz.say: If you have 7 apples and need ten, how many more do you need?
quiz.why: You count up from seven: eight, nine, ten. That is three more.

wrong.0: You might only count up one more finger.
wrong.2: You might add seven to itself.
wrong.3: You might think you need the same number.

quiz.why: When you count two and then count eight more, you reach ten.

wrong.0: Two and seven only make nine.
wrong.1: Ten is already the total, so you do not add one more.
wrong.2: Three and three only make six.
